explanation: The circular 'OK' hand sign is a well-documented obscene gesture in Brazil, historically equivalent to the middle finger — most famously when it caused a diplomatic incident after then-Vice President Richard Nixon flashed it to a crowd in Rio de Janeiro in 1958 and was met with boos. Awareness of the American 'okay' meaning has spread, especially among younger, internationally-connected Brazilians, so the gesture is somewhat less universally shocking today, but it still carries the vulgar meaning for most locals and is best avoided.
local_tip: Avoid making the circular OK sign in Brazil — use a thumbs-up instead to signal approval or that something is fine.

also_check.note: The sign is read as a vulgar insult, historically implying homosexuality as a slur.
Commonly used to mean 'okay' or 'good,' though it can look dismissive if used in place of a verbal answer.
